claim: Registered project installations can publish capability-free Ed25519 approvals for one exact relay action and registry revision. Independent approvals converge and reopen offline; expiry and same-signer equivocation are excluded from active intent counts. The relay does not yet install or enforce a signer/quorum policy.
proved: A separately domain-scoped native Ed25519 command signs project, room, exact registry revision, action hash, approval time, bounded expiry, and a 32-byte nonce.
WebCrypto independently verifies the Rust-produced signature and rejects mutations to project, revision, action hash, expiry, and nonce.
Strict Yjs records accept only unconflicted registered project-device keys, cap 500 approvals and 2,000 settings, and verify in batches of eight.
Two disconnected registered installations approving one exact action converge into one two-signer intent and reopen from a full Yjs update.
Expired approvals do not count. A signer approving two different actions at one room revision is retained for inspection but excluded from every active intent.
Read-only research-state inspection returns only counts, expected revision, action kind, and the explicit not-configured-at-relay state.
notProved: Relay-side signer-set or quorum-policy installation, proof-bundle verification, or mutation refusal.
That a registered installation belongs to an authenticated person or organization or that its participant claim is truthful.
Trusted time, approval withdrawal, deletion resistance, completeness, or availability against a Yjs writer.
Product proposal/approval interaction, packaged physical two-install behavior, or public WSS operation.
